title: Computational Cognitive Modeling (NYU DS-GA 1016 / PSYCH-GA 3405.004), Fall 2026 course site and notes
description: Graduate course site for the Fall 2026 offering taught by Todd Gureckis (lectures on Thursdays, labs on Mondays). It surveys computational frameworks for human cognition: neural networks and deep learning; reinforcement learning (introduction; exploration, generalisation and deep RL; planning and model-based RL); Bayesian models and approximate inference; model comparison and fitting; categories and concepts; structured models of reasoning; symbolic models and the language of thought; curiosity and active learning; physical and social reasoning. The site holds the syllabus, lecture and lab schedules, draft course-note chapters by Todd M. Gureckis, interactive tools (including Conway's Game of Life, an IAC model, a neuron sandbox and a Bayesian number game), lab slides and final-project guidance. The four Python homeworks are distributed only through the NYU JupyterHub.

limitations: The course is in progress: lectures from 29 October 2026 onward list no reading, and every course-note chapter opened is marked 'DRAFT' and says it 'should not be considered complete or accurate'. Content may change at the same URLs.

No lecture slides or recordings are linked from the schedule. Lab slides are linked for three labs; the PDF of the model-fitting lab returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-31 while its HTML slide page returned 200.
This offering's homework notebooks are not public. Public homework notebooks exist for the Spring 2024 offering (record lake-gureckis-ccm-2024).
Only three of the eleven course-note chapters were opened, two of them only in part; the others are known by title only.

A separate undergraduate course, Computational Cognitive Science (PSYCH-UA 300-011, Spring 2026, co-taught with Mark Ho), lives at teaching.gureckislab.org/compcogsci/; only its syllabus was opened and it is not part of this record.
